ISIS and Cyber Warfare

By: Jane Lipman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on Carte Blanche we look at the next frontier in warfare , cyberwarfare and anyone could be a target .

Summary:
Carte Blanche looks at the next frontier in warfare, its cyberwarfare , and anyone could be a target . As ISIS uses telegram , twitter , facebook and encrypted communication to spread their message we ask how real the situation is ? How scared should we be ? How does cyberwarfare play itself out ? We talk to Sizwe Snail , a cyberwarefare lawyer,Dr Jabu Mtsweni from the Cyber Research Defence Group at the CSIR , a South African representative from Anonymous , the global hacktivist group and Craig Rosewarne , a Johannesburg based cyber warfare expert . On line attacks can bring down a countrys financial systems , on line recruitment of ISIS soldiers who are cyber savvy is leading to a scenario where disasters can happen more easily ....we examine just how bad it could get

Mr. Sizwe Snail ka Mtuze
Mr. Craig Rosewarne

Script:


CYBER WARS SCRIPT

The world watches anxiously as the war between ISIS and the global coalition of countries continues to play out with frightening violent attacks . ISIS and Anonymous, an internet vigilante group of ordinary citizens , and other groups like the US based Ghost Security Group ,are using cyberwarfare and encrypted internet messaging against each other . The messages of propaganda and counter propaganda reverberate daily .
ANONYMOUS sound up
Hello Citizens of the world , we are Anonymous . The aftermath of Friday ,November 13 , 2015 France is shocked by the events caused by terrorism in the capital . We first wish to express our sorrow and solidarity with the victims , the injured and their families . To defend our values and our freedom we are tracking down members of the terrorist group responsible for these attacks .We will not give up . We will not forgive .
Anonymous continue to work against ISIS around the clock , claiming they have taken down 20,000 Twitter and Facebook accounts since November 13 .
Craig EXPERT
The challenge is you never know where they are , they don’t have to operate by any sort of laws or rules or ethics , they can typically do as they want which gives them a very wide berth of operation, in essence a very dangerous and formidable enemy to have against you .
JABU SOUND UP
Anonymous, what they are trying to do is to say if we can hack ISIS or stop them from using some of these social media they are dependent on we might sort of stop them on their tracks ….
Cyber Crime lawyer Sizwe Snail Ka Mtuze believes Anonymous are on line Robin Hoods
So Anonymous have declared war on ISIS , what does that actually mean?
They will go out of their way to use their expertise in the cyber security world to maybe assist law enforcement agencies to expose particular cells , to give certain intel , to certain military establishments

Bongani LINK The world as we once knew it has changed , the cyber age has brought many benefits including our global sense of interconnected ness ,but it has also left us vulnerable in ways we haven’t begun to imagine
Millions of cyber attacks happen every day. Some American Defence experts claim that cyber warfare is now critical to all their military operations and billions of dollars are spent on cyber security at sites like the National Security Agency in Maryland in the United States .

The NSA examine claims such as that ISIS use online gaming to get contacts. Its suspected that online games can be used as an undercover communications device and ISIS MAY be able to target the game players as recruits for their jihad to create a caliphate . It is notoriously hard to monitor on line gaming activities .
Meanwhile the daily battles between IS and Anonymous are via hacking,the destruction of information and bringing down websites , twitter accounts and facebook accounts . Leaving ISIS on the defence having to adapt .
JABU They are always changing their modus operandi , after Snowden leaks in the US , so they would understand for example how the state security are actually collecting information and then they will change from that . Before they might be using Twitter , nowadays they might be using that less because they know that NSA or whoever , has access to that information ,and they now may be using custom tools that they can build for themselves .


BONGANI stand up There are over eleven million facebook users in South Africa , six million of us tweet , but those number are dwarfed in comparison with the social media penetration we see in Europe and with so many people on line its not hard to find marginalised and disaffected youth to recruit for groups like ISIS .

Voice
According to its website , Telegram is a secure private communications and messaging application that can allow messages to be destroyed within 60 seconds.
Sound up Jabu Mtsweni
They use the social media for various things , for example for either recruiting the people that they want them to join for propaganda you know for broadcasting some of their victories if you want to call them that ,and they use other tools like in the Paris attack , called the Telegram , they have used that to actually even broadcast to everyone , when they were claiming responsibility , we are the ones who did this .

Of course they use it because within that particular space chances of them being traced are very limited compared to lets say “Whats App” because that APP would consider privacy and anonymity more than the other app would .

In the shady , seedy back alleys of the internet is the dark web with secretive networks and browsers like TOR , that people can use without being traced .Its a deep digital space that allows criminals to operate undetected .

Jabu you know just like TOR , TOR which is in the dark net was actually developed by the US government and they developed it for them to communicate privately , but the criminals then they take it and they use it for something that it was not intended for .
Brian Dube is the Head of Communications at State Security

There is some work there but its not necessarily bad that happens there . But overall what we do there because it’s a very technical aspect of that work , there is work we are doing in terms of sharing information , with INTEPOL for instance . Intepol has got a dedicated program that looks at such things , how we identify these criminals .

In 2007 the websites of the mainly on line Government of Estonia came under attack for three weeks .They were bombarded by mass requests for information and then couldn’t access their emails or run the government or banking systems .The attacks were reported to be linked to a dispute between Russia and Estonia .
PUT IN FLAGS HERE

Bongani question Are we likely to see groups like ISIS targeting infrastructure , hacking into electricity grids , like they did in Estonia ?
Brian Dube
Well its important to indicate that there is no country which is immune from these things . Essentially we cant claim that it can never happen here .
There are risk and data recovery strategies we have in place , in terms of our systems , our critical infrastructure for instance , how do we ensure there are back up systems , how do we ensure there are recovery systems off site so that if we were to be hit by a disaster for instance , whether natural or terrorist related whatever we would be able to minimise the impact thereof .
Government says our information technology systems are able to pick up cyber attacks, and once they are identified , they can defend the country against the onslaught , and with care , stop the spread of any damage .

Voice over : However globally many experts are predicting that the next major attack will be digital and could be more devastating than 9 / 11.
Bongani question: Why is no body stopping them ?
Jabu answer “ We are always behind , criminals they tend to be one step ahead, but the other issue is about information sharing .We don’t share a lot , amongst ourselves , I mean the people who are trying to protect the systems in the country , so we don’t share a lot ,also the issue that the data is growing at a very faster pace , so its very difficult with the current systems that we have to keep up .
LINK BONGANI Theres a great deal of mistrust between countries and as a result and as a result there isnt a lot of information sharing going on and increasingly theres a realisation that this needs to change .


Craig “ if you bring down the Reserve bank or the Joburg Stock Exchange or the Banking system , you will wreak havoc on a country’s economy , you cant draw their money out and people are going to start going crazy , bring down the water systems , theres sewage systems for example involved , everything is controlled by computers nowadays .
Voice over
Recently the British government have been taking cyber warfare very seriously with the announcement of a NEW Cyber defence centre in the UK at their Government Communications Headquarters . Chancellor George Osborne is spending 1.9 billion pounds on the new centre , saying that whatever is online is now a target .
Our govern ment says that they are not far behind with a whole NEW way of thinking about defence .The new cyber security hub at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research is in Pretoria . …..
Dube
Those who want to hack in to the systems would always try to hack from the weaker points so to speak and then gain entry into the broader system as it were .
So government says theres no need to panic , its systems are quite secure and they can detect any cyber attacks that are coming at them .
Jabu You know theres a platform we are working on, a cyber threat intelligence platform , which we are building it to try and bring intelligence organisations together , to share information , but in a very trusted community ,because again when you are sharing you don’t want to be sharing in a public platform where everyone would now be able to know , OK company A , company B was attacked and so on and so forth .

BONGANI VOICE it’s a scary world of cyber terrorism and warfare where to avoid being a target you need to have a fast turnaround development of counter technology . The question is , is it too late?

metadata.Summary: Carte Blanche looks at the next frontier in warfare, its cyberwarfare , and anyone could be a target . As ISIS uses telegram , twitter , facebook and encrypted communication to spread their message we ask how real the situation is ? How scared should we be ? How does cyberwarfare play itself out ? We talk to Sizwe Snail , a cyberwarefare lawyer,Dr Jabu Mtsweni from the Cyber Research Defence Group at the CSIR , a South African representative from Anonymous , the global hacktivist group and Craig Rosewarne , a Johannesburg based cyber warfare expert . On line attacks can bring down a countrys financial systems , on line recruitment of ISIS soldiers who are cyber savvy is leading to a scenario where disasters can happen more easily ....we examine just how bad it could get
